sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the allegory of the beast and bird from the Gemara, relating them to the coarse and refined levels of the animal soul.

translations.translation: And this can be explained according to what is stated in the Gemara:
A beast that was created from dry land is kosher with two signs, etc.; a bird that was created from marshland is kosher with one sign.
And it is explained elsewhere,
that a beast created from dust
(dry land)
—therefore it has healthy and strong vitality—
alludes to the animal soul as it is in the strength of coarseness.
Therefore its kosher status requires two signs.
And a bird created from marshland,
water and dust,
alludes to the animal soul as it is in refinement.
Therefore its kosher status requires one sign.
And in more detail:
The beast is the animal soul
(itself),
which is from the lower levels of Nogah
(its coarseness),
and the bird is the intellectual soul, which is from the higher levels of Nogah
(its refinement),
therefore it is an intermediary
between the animal soul and the G-dly soul.
And this is that the bird flies in the air
(from time to time),
for this can be explained in two ways.
The flight in the air
(of the bird)
is from the side of the intellectual soul itself.
For the nature of the intellect
(even the intellect of the intellectual soul, although it is natural intellect,
intellect of Nogah,
nevertheless,
since it is intellect,
its nature)
is to be drawn after that which is above it.
And there is another aspect in this:
that through the clothing of the G-dly soul in the intellectual soul,
it is able to apprehend matters of G-dliness that are above the world.
However, even then it only agrees to the apprehension of the G-dly soul, but it remains in its essence—human intellect.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains why guarding birds requires a covered courtyard, as the refined evil of Nogah is less noticeable and the intellectual soul's tendency to soar requires greater protection.

translations.translation: And it can be said,
that this [law]—that guarding beasts is also in an uncovered courtyard, while guarding birds is specifically in a covered courtyard
(even though birds are more refined)—
is because the refinement of Nogah is not so noticeable,
and therefore requires greater guarding.
And to add:
Just as in the physical,
the reason that birds are not guarded in an uncovered courtyard is because they can fly
(over the partitions),
so too is it in spirituality:
that the intellectual soul requires greater guarding because it has the characteristic of flight in the air.
That is,
since the intellect of the intellectual soul is drawn after that which is above it
[and moreover,
it apprehends
(through the clothing of the G-dly soul in the intellectual soul)
matters of G-dliness that are above the world],
therefore,
in order to find the evil in the intellect, it is specifically through contemplation that G-dliness is hidden from human intellect
[i.e., even the matters of G-dliness that are apprehended in human intellect,
the intellect does not grasp them as they are in their truth,
for since they are G-dliness,
they are without limit,
and as the intellect grasps them,
it necessarily limits them],
and through the intellectual soul
(bird)
feeling the hiddenness of G-dliness that is above intellect,
[being] covered by a roof,
through this the refined evil within it is clarified,
[and] it is guarded.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the law of an uncovered courtyard being a karmelit is rabbinic, because guarding the beast (action) is biblical, while guarding the bird (intellect) requires a roof to refine pride, a rabbinic enhancement.

translations.translation: And based on this, we can explain that the law that an uncovered courtyard is a karmelit is rabbinic,
for guarding the beast
(in the service of man)
is primarily regarding thought, speech, and action,
for from the desires of the animal soul one might stumble into some prohibition, G-d forbid,
and guarding the beast is by fencing the courtyard
(the place where the beast is located)
with partitions,
i.e., not doing what he wants, but only what he must do.
And guarding the bird
(in the service of man)
which is regarding the refinement of Nogah
(as above)
is primarily regarding the inner powers,
intellect and emotions.
For from the selfhood and pride within him
(from his being a man of intellect,
"seeing a wise man in his own eyes"),
it is not sufficient to fence the courtyard with partitions,
for even when he is bounded in his thought, speech, and action,
even to the level of a Beinoni who never committed a transgression in his life,
nevertheless,
from the pride and coarseness within him,
his intellect and emotions are in coarseness,
and therefore his courtyard must be covered with a roof,
so that the hiddenness of G-dliness is felt within him, as above.
And since the main thing is action,
therefore,
biblically, even an uncovered courtyard is a private domain,
the Unique One of the world,
but rabbinically
[whose function is to elevate and raise the person,
so that he becomes a vessel for G-dliness also from the side of his intellect and emotions],
in order for a person to be a private domain for His uniqueness, it is through [the courtyard] being covered with a roof.
